content.title: Tiger Woods’ history of car crashes and injuries: What to know after latest DUI arrest
content.text: Tiger Woods was arrested and jailed on charges of driving under the influence following a two-car crash Friday near Woods’ home in Jupiter Island, Fla.The Jupiter Island Police Department responded to calls about a rollover crash on South Beach Road just before 2 p.m. ET. A pickup truck pulling a trailer fitted for a pressure cleaner was attempting to turn left on a two-lane road when a Land Rover, driven by Woods, attempted to overtake the truck at high speed, Martin County Sheriff John M. Budensiek said during a news conference Friday. The pickup truck made efforts to edge off to the side of the road, seeing Woods’ vehicle in his rearview mirror, but there was no shoulder on the small two-lane road. Woods overtook the pickup truck at the last moment, clipping the back end of the trailer.Woods’ car subsequently rolled in the direction of the driver’s door and slid northbound, according to Budensiek. Woods was able to crawl out of the passenger door after the crash. There is a 30 mph speed limit on South Beach Road, but Budensiek said it was not known what speed Woods was traveling at the time of the crash.Woods passed a breathalyzer exam but refused a urinalysis, triggering the charge of DUI with property damage. He was also charged with refusal to submit to a lawful test, Budensiek said. Both charges are misdemeanors.The crash is the fourth major incident involving Woods and an automobile, all since 2009. The total effect of these incidents has caused personal, physical and professional harm to Woods, 50.2009: Tiger hits fire hydrantOn Nov. 27, 2009, Woods crashed his SUV into a fire hydrant and a tree outside of his home near Orlando, Fla., at 2:30 a.m. The Florida Highway Patrol responded to the incident and found Woods with lacerations on his face. His wife at the time, Elin Nordegren, was at the scene, helping Woods. She told officers she used a golf club to break the vehicle’s rear window to help Woods out of the car.Woods was found to be at fault in the incident, but did not face charges beyond a traffic citation for careless driving, according to the Florida Highway Patrol. The crash occurred two days after a tabloid first published reports of Woods’ infidelity. After the crash, more reports followed, which Woods ultimately publicly apologized for. He subsequently took an extended break from professional golf and was divorced from Nordegren in 2010.It was the first public fall from grace for Woods, who had won 14 major championships from 1997 to 2008 and seemed primed to reset the golf history book. He’s won one major since, the 2019 Masters, and is tied with Sam Snead for most PGA Tour victories.2017: Found asleep in a vehicleOn May 29, 2017, Woods was arrested in Jupiter, Fla., on suspicion of driving under the influence. Police found him asleep in his black Mercedes at 3 a.m, stopped in the right lane. The engine of Woods’ car was still running. Woods ultimately pleaded guilty to reckless driving, but explained that the incident was due to an “unexpected reaction” to multiple prescription drugs in his system at once, including Vicodin, Dilaudid, Xanax, Ambien and THC. Woods said that he was self-medicating for pain following his spinal fusion in April 2017. His breathalyzer test was negative (0.00) on the scene. Following the incident, Woods completed a DUI diversion program.Tiger Woods’ vehicle after he was involved in a rollover crash in Rancho Palos Verdes. Emergency personnel used the “jaws of life” to remove him from the vehicle.Harrison Hill / USA Today Sports Images2021: Life-threatening car crash in Los AngelesOn Feb, 23, 2021, Woods was speeding on a winding road near Los Angeles at more than 80 mph when he crashed his Genesis SUV in a near-fatal single-car crash. He was headed to a content photoshoot, just three months removed from his latest back surgery — a microdiscectomy.Aerial video of the crash scene showed Woods crossed over a median, the vehicle struck a tree, and it was sent into the air, landing in brush nearby. Los Angeles County Sheriff Alex Villanueva said that there were no signs of impairment, and Woods was wearing his seatbelt. Investigators said they believed Woods accidentally stepped on the accelerator when he meant to press the brake pedal. Woods suffered extensive injuries from the crash, including significant damage to his right leg and ankle. His bone broke through the skin, and doctors performed immediate emergency surgery. He also shattered his talus bone in his ankle.“I’m lucky to be alive and also have a limb,” Woods told reporters in November 2021 at the Hero World Challenge.Fallout from the 2021 crashFollowing the crash, Woods underwent multiple surgeries and procedures relating to the original trauma. He battled plantar fasciitis in his right foot in late 2022, later opting for a subtalar ankle fusion to address arthritis in the area. Between procedures, Woods returned to competitive golf. He teed it up in the 2022 Masters and made the cut, finishing in 47th place, but withdrew from the PGA Championship and missed the cut at The Open Championship. He withdrew from the 2023 Masters, leading to the right ankle surgery.Woods last competed in a major tournament at The Open Championship in 2024. Following that tournament, in September 2024, Woods underwent a microdecompression for his sixth back surgery. While training at home to make another comeback to competitive golf in 2025, Woods injured himself again — this time, he ruptured his left Achilles tendon. Woods’ latest procedure came in October 2025. He underwent a lumbar disc replacement, marking his seventh back surgery since 2014.On Tuesday, Woods made his first public appearance swinging a golf club since that disc replacement at TGL, the indoor simulator golf league he co-founded. He had not announced a decision on playing in the 2026 Masters, which starts on April 8. Woods was slated to appear in Augusta for the annual Champions Dinner, as well as the re-opening of the Augusta Municipal Golf Course.
